findings.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:92 — Guests are committed before the external calendar update, so a calendar failure leaves persisted guests despite returning an error and retries can duplicate the operation.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:167 — Email delivery failures are swallowed and the mutation reports success, silently leaving organizers and attendees without required guest-change notifications.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts:5 — The guest array has no size limit, allowing any attendee to trigger unbounded inserts, translation loads, calendar payload growth, and email fan-out in one request.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:74 — Filtering does not deduplicate guests within the submitted array, so repeated addresses can create duplicate attendee rows and duplicate downstream notifications.

goldens.comment: The addGuests.handler.ts blacklist check uses blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) after lowercasing the blacklist but not the input guest emails, allowing attackers to bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS restrictions by submitting emails with uppercase characters.

The logic for checking team admin/owner permissions is incorrect. This condition uses AND (&&) which requires both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to be true, but it should use OR (||) since a user needs to be either an admin OR an owner to have permission.

The sendAddGuestsEmails function in email-manager.ts passes the full calendarEvent.attendees array when determining which attendees receive AttendeeScheduledEmail vs AttendeeAddGuestsEmail, but checks if newGuests.includes(attendee.email) where newGuests is the input guests array.

uniqueGuests filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails but does not deduplicate duplicates within the input; createMany can insert duplicate attendee rows if the client submits repeated emails.
Starting with an array containing an empty string may cause validation issues. Consider starting with an empty array [] and handling the empty state in the MultiEmail component instead.

The `sendAddGuestsEmails` function does not check the `disableStandardEmails` flags in the `EventType` metadata, which may result in sending emails to hosts/attendees even when standard emails are disabled for the event type.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:92 — Guests are committed before the external calendar update, so a calendar failure leaves persisted guests despite returning an error and retries can duplicate the operation.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the addGuests.handler.ts code, the flow is: 1) prisma.booking.update adds guests to DB (line 92-106), 2) eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees updates external calendar (line 161), 3) sendAddGuestsEmails sends emails (line 165). If updateCalendarAttendees fails, it would throw an error, but the guests are already persisted in the database. This is a real atomicity issue - the database write succeeds but the external calendar update could fail, leaving the system in an inconsistent state where guests exist in the booking but not in the external calendar. The finding correctly identifies this as a potential problem with the transaction ordering.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:167 — Email delivery failures are swallowed and the mutation reports success, silently leaving organizers and attendees without required guest-change notifications.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at lines 165-169 in addGuests.handler.ts, the code catches email sending errors and only logs 'Error sending AddGuestsEmails' to console, then continues to return success with { message: 'Guests added' }. This means if email delivery fails, the mutation still reports success to the user, and organizers/attendees won't receive notifications about the guest changes. The guests are already added to the database at this point (line 85-99), so the data change is committed but notifications fail silently. This is a real correctness issue - users expect that when they add guests, those guests and existing attendees will be notified. The silent failure means the feature appears to work but critical notifications may not be sent.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts:5 — The guest array has no size limit, allowing any attendee to trigger unbounded inserts, translation loads, calendar payload growth, and email fan-out in one request.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that ZAddGuestsInputSchema in addGuests.schema.ts defines `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` with no maximum length constraint. Looking at addGuests.handler.ts, each guest triggers: 1) database inserts via createMany, 2) translation loads via getTranslation for each attendee, 3) calendar updates via eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees, and 4) email sending via sendAddGuestsEmails which fans out to organizer, team members, and all attendees. An attacker who is an attendee of a booking could submit thousands of guest emails in a single request, causing significant resource consumption. This is a real security/DoS concern - the schema should have a reasonable .max() constraint.
